sentences.text: Social worker Tom Ashby identified himself as being from the adult team at Coldmere and stated they had previously spoken on the phone.
Lisa Keegan, identified as the person's daughter, stated she had taken the morning off.
Ronald Keegan agreed to Lisa Keegan staying while the social worker spoke with him.
The hospital requested the social worker to visit after Ronald Keegan's fall to assess his management and potential needs.
Ronald Keegan stated Pat was his wife for forty-six years and died last March.
Ronald Keegan described his condition since returning home from Coldmere General Hospital as 'not bad' but noted he felt 'bit stiff' and his hip was sore when going up stairs.
Ronald Keegan stated he goes up the stairs 'on his backside some nights' and noted there is only one handrail.
Ronald Keegan stated he cannot get into the bath since the fall.
Ronald Keegan stated he has a strip wash.
Ronald Keegan stated he microwaves dinners.
Ronald Keegan stated his wife, Pat, cooked all the meals.
Ronald Keegan stated it is quiet without his wife Pat.
Ronald Keegan stated he watches telly, specifically 'the racing'.
Ronald Keegan stated he used to go to the British Legion on Fridays but has not bothered lately.
Ronald Keegan stated he wants to stay in his house and does not want a home.
Ronald Keegan admitted he likes a drink and will not lie, stating he has 'a couple of cans' of an evening and 'a couple of cans with my tea'.
Lisa Keegan stated the alcohol consumption is not a couple of cans, but eight cans a day of the big strong lager, which she counts in the recycling bin every Sunday.
Lisa Keegan stated there is also vodka, noting he gets a bottle from Spar that goes in two days.
Lisa Keegan confirmed she sees the empty cans in the bin every Sunday and has counted them.
Ronald Keegan disputed Lisa's count, stating it is only a couple of cans and that he is not drunk or hurting anybody.
Lisa Keegan stated she found Ronald Keegan in the morning after he had been drinking since dinner time.
Lisa Keegan stated Ronald Keegan fell in the kitchen while on the floor all night and could not get up.
Lisa Keegan stated this was not the first time, noting he fell in the hall in the summer after having a drink.
Ronald Keegan stated the previous fall was on the step.
Mrs Okafor, next door, told Lisa Keegan she saw Ronald Keegan driving to the Co-op after he had had a drink.
Lisa Keegan stated she has not seen Ronald Keegan driving herself as she is at work.
Ronald Keegan disputed Mrs Okafor's claim, stating he only drives on Sundays to the cemetery and that she wants to mind her own business.
The social worker noted Mrs Okafor's statement to Lisa Keegan and Ronald Keegan's dispute of that statement.
Ronald Keegan stated he has the state pension and a works pension from the foundry, totaling about fourteen hundred a month.
Ronald Keegan stated he has never heard of Attendance Allowance.
